title: UK Airline Offers to Pay for Babies' First Passports
paragraphs: Going on holiday with a baby for the first time can be exciting, but it can also be expensive. Now, a British airline company is offering to pay for babies' first passports.

In October 2026, easyJet holidays, the holiday company of the airline easyJet, announced the offer for customers in the UK. A child's first passport costs £66.50 if parents apply online, so the company is giving a discount of £66.50 on holiday bookings.

However, there are some conditions. The offer is only for holidays, not for flights alone. It is for one baby per booking, and the baby must be under 18 months old when the holiday is booked. The baby must also be under two years old when the family travels. Customers must book before November 26, 2026, and they must travel before October 31, 2028. Parents still have to pay for the passport themselves first.

Getting a passport for a baby can be difficult. Parents need two photos of the baby, and they also need someone who has known them for at least two years to confirm the baby's identity. In the UK, a child's passport lasts for five years.

easyJet holidays also carried out a survey of 2,000 British parents who had traveled abroad with a child under five. In the survey, 82% said the trip was an important family moment, and 87% said they would do it again. In addition, 48% said that traveling with a baby was easier than they had expected.
According to the company, the number of babies traveling on its holidays in 2026 had already risen 10% compared with 2025, with two months of the year still left.
Stuart Wright of easyJet holidays said, "Travel has a unique way of bringing families together." He said the offer would help families start making memories "that little bit sooner."
